Twitter is a multiplayer real-time virtual world, primarily text-based with limited multimedia support. It combines elements of role-playing games, hack and slash, player versus player, interactive fiction, and online chat.
↓
1094687116796125186 [2019-02-10] @visakanv 💜 193 🔁 10
Players can read, view and contribute descriptions of objects, other players, non-player characters, and actions performed in the virtual world, as well as the “real” world. Players typically interact with each other by utilizing strings that resemble a natural language.
↓
1094688015199350785 [2019-02-10] @visakanv 💜 192 🔁 20
While traditional MUDs typically implement RPGs set in distinct fantasy worlds populated by fictional races and monsters, with players choosing classes in order to gain specific skills or powers, Twitter allows every player to project their own fantasy and define their own game.
↓
1094689527615021056 [2019-02-10] @visakanv 💜 276 🔁 29
The flexible nature of Twitter makes it difficult for any singular definition of “the game” to become canonical. Conflict between players with different interpretations of Twitter is a key feature of Twitter itself. Indeed, one of the most popular games is “hey, fuck that guy”.
↓
1094691177289281536 [2019-02-10] @visakanv 💜 216 🔁 9
Unsurprisingly, few players put much thought into precisely defining the game that they are playing. Most players “pick it up” organically as they go along, inheriting the unwritten rules and norms of their peers via imitation and (limited) experimentation.
├── 1094694093509128192 [2019-02-10] @visakanv 💜 203 🔁 13
│   The key feature of (public) Twitter is that any player can interact with any other player. Any player can reply to any other player’s tweets, or retweet it, or quote-tweet it. This bypasses traditional limitations of both “real life” as well as older web mediums like “blogs”.
│   ↓
│   1094697463301079041 [2019-02-10] @visakanv 💜 195 🔁 12
│   Twitter is also searchable, and allows tweets to be “threaded” in chains. 
│   
│   This allows skilled players to build incredibly complex tapestries of hypertext, consisting of thousands of tweets.
│   ↓
│   1094698711618269184 [2019-02-10] @visakanv 💜 210 🔁 13
│   Why would such prolific players choose Twitter as a medium, rather than “websites” or “books”, which appear to be better suited to large volumes of content?
│   
│   Because Twitter allows any player to interact with any other player’s tweets.
│   ↓
│   1094699709027905545 [2019-02-10] @visakanv 💜 398 🔁 38
│   Most casual players do not appear to have caught on to the true potential utility of Twitter, or perhaps they are indifferent to it. 
│   
│   A web of tweets is a living entity that allows players to meet, interact and engage with 1000s of others *at the level of individual thoughts*.
│   ↓
│   1094701060462075904 [2019-02-10] @visakanv 💜 206 🔁 13
│   Properly constructed, a web of tweets allows you to:
│   
│   - witness how other players discover your tweets, via their patterns of Likes, RTs, QTs
│   
│   - connect each fragmented thought and experience into a part of a greater whole
│   
│   - recognise and embellish patterns in your own play
│   ↓
│   1094701702807048197 [2019-02-10] @visakanv 💜 169 🔁 8
│   We have not yet even begun talking about relationships. Players can build relationships with other players over time and shared interactions. Through cooperation, multiple players can share and merge webs with one another, helping each other find and share desired information
└── 1865972747404267803 [2024-12-09] @ultimape 💜 5

rating.reasoning_summary: This strand represents a meta-narrative about Twitter itself as a game/MMORPG, anchored by Visakanv's 2019 'twitter_rpg_strategy_guide.txt' thread. The boundary object is the conceptual frame of Twitter-as-game, which gets repeatedly cited and refined over 5+ years (2019-2024). The discourse is primarily constructive rather than dialectical—people build on the metaphor rather than challenge it. Evolution is medium: the core insight remains stable (Twitter = MMORPG), but applications deepen (threading as 'weaving webs,' micro-cultures as 'clusters,' status games as PvP). Cohesion is high—Visakanv's original thread becomes canonical, cited by multiple users across years. Utility is medium-high: it provides a practical mental model for new users and validates experienced users' intuitions, though it doesn't produce new social technology beyond the metaphor itself.

essential_tweets.annotation: The Origin: Visakanv introduces Twitter as 'multiplayer real-time virtual world' combining RPG/PvP/interactive fiction elements
Key Insight: 'Conflict between players with different interpretations of Twitter is a key feature of Twitter itself'—legitimizing meta-game awareness
The Value Prop: 'A web of tweets allows players to meet, interact and engage with 1000s of others at the level of individual thoughts'
Conclusion of original thread: 'With a little introspection, Twitter can be a tool for self-inquiry, making friends, testing ideas'
Qiaochu's complementary micro-guide: 'follow ppl whose tweets u want inside u,' 'improv not debate,' 'goddamnit be kind'
M_ashcroft's refinement: 'Twitter is an opt-in infinite improv game where the only wrong move is to try to win'—adding strategic layer
IaimforGOAT's synthesis: 'Twitter is the best open world MMORPG of all time'—validating the metaphor 3 years later with detailed exploration guide
Cluster Theory: 'You are free to enter any micro culture...figure out their values, lingo, lore'—applying RPG frame to social navigation
Eshear's compression: 'Twitter is the Calvinball of MMORPGs'—capturing the rule-fluidity insight in one metaphor
Bashu's 2024 tactical insight: 'there is a mana bar...depletes as you become enraged...replenishes by having nice conversations'—operationalizing the game mechanics

title: Twitter Is an MMORPG—and rage drains your mana
summary:
The most useful twist in this whole “Twitter is a game” saga is @bashu_thanks’ 2024 patch note: you *start to win* when you notice your “mana bar” depletes every time you get enraged by dipshits, and refills when you have nice conversations with smart/kind people. It takes @visakanv’s original 2019 “twitter_rpg_strategy_guide.txt” metaphor (Twitter as a text-based multiplayer world with PvP) and turns it into an actual playstyle: stop spending spell slots on outrage, spec into conviviality.

This all kicks off with @visakanv framing Twitter as a “multiplayer real-time virtual world” where everyone projects their own fantasy and the *conflict between interpretations* is the point—his most quotable line is basically “Twitter can’t have one canonical ruleset, so fighting about what Twitter ‘is’ becomes the game.” The thread peaks when he sells the real mechanic: threading/search makes “a web of tweets… a living entity” that lets you meet thousands of people “at the level of individual thoughts,” not just audience blobs. After that, the idea becomes a roaming meme + manual: @QiaochuYuan drops the gentle micro-meta (“improv, not debate” and “goddamnit, be kind”), @m_ashcroft refines it into strategy (“opt-in infinite improv game” where “the only wrong move is to try to win”), and the edgelord builds roll in—@eigenrobot wants bluechecks to “drop gear” and calls it a global PvP server. Then @IaimforGOAT writes the open-world guide version: Twitter’s fun is hopping “micro cultures / clusters,” learning each one’s “values, lingo, lore,” and using the algorithm like fast-travel to find your people.

It doesn’t really “end”—it keeps resurfacing whenever someone needs a coping frame—until @eshear compresses the whole thing into one perfect joke (“Twitter is the Calvinball of MMORPGs”), and then @bashu_thanks adds the first genuinely actionable HUD element (mana). You’d care because this metaphor is basically a survival guide: it explains why Twitter constantly feels like a rules dispute + bar fight, and it gives you permission to treat it like a world you can explore, curate, and exit—rather than a tribunal you have to “win.”
